Three retirements in this bundle remove the `validate` job's need for full history — that control, the direct full-history assertion, and the declaration-count coverage guard — so the job currently carries `fetch-depth: 0` and `scripts/audit-regressions.test.ts` carries a static guard that reddens when the depth is not full. It also retires the declaration-count coverage guard and answers applied `AC-COVERAGE-INTACT`. **This explicitly overturns** `AC-MINT-EXCLUSIVE`'s isolated-baseline control and `AC-BASELINE-CONTROL-AVAILABLE` in `.ngrace/changes/archive/C-SUPERSEDE-MEMBERSHIP-4-20941257/spec.xml` and `.ngrace/changes/archive/C-LINUX-VALIDATION-REPAIR-5-EE982B6D/spec.xml` (applied successor `C-LINUX-VALIDATION-REPAIR-6-62765C22`), `AC-WORKFLOW-FULL-HISTORY` in the same files, `AC-COVERAGE-INTACT` in `.ngrace/changes/archive/C-TEST-TIME-BUDGET-4-F173437E/spec.xml`, and the `C-SQUASH-WITNESS-1-87D77A3D` NonGoal `The mint-exclusive control against 6dd1d95 … stays`; the reasoning is in `Problem`. Base commit `80cc36f789dc35ef789cfe6d753a39e7115dce76` (the separate docs-only commit). No production source, skill, or CLI byte changes. `mint-search: 0 active, 0 archive prior bundle(s) share slug MINT-BASELINE-CONTROL` (the value printed at mint, carried verbatim).

Goals.Goal: **Remove the permanent historical baseline control.** `src/grace-generate.test.ts` no longer holds the `BASE_COMMIT` constant (`6dd1d95`) or the detached-worktree test, and no ordinary test run checks out an ancestor commit. The interceptor `describe` block stays; the repaired-tree race test, the two exported-route tests, and the implicit-supersede CLI test stay.

**Keep the current-code control discriminating.** The retained race test drives the real `ngrace spec new` CLI against a disposable project, plants a competitor between the existence check and directory creation with an isolated-process interceptor, requires the interceptor to report it fired, requires a non-zero exit, and requires the competitor's `spec.xml` and its unrelated file to survive byte-for-byte. The implicit-supersede test drives the real `ngrace supersede` CLI the same way. The two exported-route tests spawn Bun runners that import `mintResolvedBundle` and `mintBundle` directly and repeat the refusal and byte preservation.

**Substitute a one-time red control for the permanent old-code checkout.** On a disposable non-Git copy, the pre-repair defect (`mkdirSync(bundlePath, { recursive: true })` plus the non-exclusive spec write) is planted and the retained race test must redden; the copy is restored byte-identical and the retained race test must green. The control is not added to the suite and `src/grace-generate.test.ts` gains no planted-defect test.

**Remove the full-history assertion and the full-history checkout.** `scripts/audit-regressions.test.ts` removes the `validateJobCheckoutDepth` helper and the test titled `the validate job checks out full history for the pinned baseline control`; that assertion hard-fails if the workflow drops `fetch-depth: 0` while it remains. The same file retains the README fail-closed-candidate guard. The `validate` job's Checkout step in `.github/workflows/validate.yml` carries no `fetch-depth` key.

**Retire the declaration-count coverage guard and answer its archived criterion.** `scripts/audit-regressions.test.ts` removes `COVERAGE_BASE`, `declaredTests`, `coverageRegressions`, and the `C-TEST-TIME-BUDGET-2-3EC1F016 coverage never falls` describe/test, while retaining `collectTestFiles` (used by `findTimeoutPins`) and the unrelated `validate:ci` one-suite-run guard (`validateCiRerunsSuite`). The spec answers applied `AC-COVERAGE-INTACT` of `C-TEST-TIME-BUDGET-4-F173437E`: the guard counted textual `it(`/`test(` declarations, not executed code, and it failed open in a shallow checkout; no broad suite-wide coverage floor remains, the targeted mint test does not replace one, and measured executed-code coverage is deferred to a later, separate bundle.

**Keep the metric artifact honest to the post-change population.** `test-metrics.json` names no test that this bundle removed and still names every `.test.ts` under `src/` and `scripts/`. `artifactIsStale` of the repository against it is false.

**Overturn the archived criteria with their reasoning answered.** The permanent old-code control was installed by accepted criteria; this bundle states that it overturns them, cites each, and explains why the retained current-code race test plus a one-time red control suffices. It does not silently edit archives.

**Whole-consumer search for `fetch-depth: 0` in the `validate` job.** Official `actions/checkout` documentation states that `fetch-depth: 0` fetches all history for all branches and tags, so a fresh checkout carries a commit only when some ref reaches it; presence is a reachability fact, not an ancestry fact, and absence is never inferred here from non-ancestry. Measured 2026-09-28 UTC in this clone: `git cat-file -e` succeeds for `b53d13df47cdf8d85f75b33502c6ecd9e97ff262`, `0fbd59961d15b7587cc2b153e225fcdcf9066db2`, `73044f83c3f4eaaaa5c5b7648a8a31c115337c39`, and `2434fd467458e15c12414a74e37b09f9d71bdfd2`, while `git for-each-ref --contains` reaches a current ref for none of the first three and does reach `2434fd4…` (an ancestor of `HEAD` via `main`). **Three retirements together remove the job's need for full history; the earlier claim that the mint control alone was the only hard consumer was wrong.** (1) The removed historical mint worktree test hard-fails without the object: `git worktree add --detach … 6dd1d95`, and `6dd1d95` is reachable from `HEAD`/`main`, so `fetch-depth: 0` fetches it and a depth-1 checkout does not. (2) The removed `validateJobCheckoutDepth` assertion hard-fails if `.github/workflows/validate.yml` drops `fetch-depth: 0` while the assertion remains; it asserts the key directly and reads no historical object. (3) The removed coverage declaration-count guard (`coverageRegressions`, `scripts/audit-regressions.test.ts:346`) reads `git show 2434fd4…:<path>` for every existing `*.test.ts` and **fails open**: on a non-zero `git show` it `continue`s (`:352`), so in a depth-1 checkout (base object absent) it silently reports no regression — a false green — while after the object is fetched it reddens on a dropped declaration. The audited remaining `validate:ci` consumers do **not** hard-require full history: `scripts/validate-marketplace.ts` `getChangedFiles` widens to scope-`all` on a failed history diff; `b53d13d…`/`0fbd5996…` tolerate absence with a named reason; `73044f83…` is the dormant close-time scope-guard base that refuses only when explicitly activated without evidence; and the archive/`git show HEAD` reads need only `HEAD`. The optional `test:affected` and release paths are outside `validate:ci` and are not consumers of the job's depth. Removing the mint control, the depth assertion, and the count guard is therefore one coherent change. Leave the publish workflow's own `fetch-depth: 0` untouched.

**The one-time red control stays out of the suite.** `src/grace-generate.test.ts` gains no test that plants the pre-repair defect, and no permanent test references `BASE_COMMIT`, `6dd1d95`, or `git worktree`. The red-control transcript (the mutation, the observed red, the byte-identical restore, the observed green) is recorded in `design-context.xml` and reported by the executor; it is evidence, not a suite member. A probe that only observes green is not the control: the red direction must be driven.

(c) `C-SQUASH-WITNESS-1-87D77A3D` NonGoal `The mint-exclusive control against 6dd1d95 … stays`. (d) `AC-COVERAGE-INTACT` (`.ngrace/changes/archive/C-TEST-TIME-BUDGET-4-F173437E/spec.xml`) required the declaration-count guard; it is answered in `Problem` item 6 and retired by `AC-COVERAGE-GUARD-RETIRED`. The original argument was **discrimination**: without a known-bad tree, a green refusal test could be vacuous. The counter-argument to removing it is that the permanent checkout is cheap because `6dd1d95` is an ancestor of `HEAD`, and that its guard protects a live mechanism. **3. Why the guard and the full-history checkout can go.** `AC-WORKFLOW-FULL-HISTORY`'s guard protects a live mechanism: a reverted checkout depth would break the historical control. Once the historical control is removed, the guard has no subject and the checkout needs no full history. Once the mint control, the depth assertion, and the count guard are retired, the audited remaining `validate:ci` consumers do not hard-require full history: `validate-marketplace`'s `origin/main...HEAD` diff widens to scope-`all` on a failed history diff, `release:check` fetches `origin/main` explicitly, `b53d13d…` and `0fbd5996…` accept a named object-absence, `73044f83…` is the dormant scope-guard base that refuses only when explicitly activated without evidence, and the archive/`git show HEAD` reads need only `HEAD`. The optional `test:affected` and release paths are outside `validate:ci` and are not consumers of the job's depth. Removing the three is therefore one coherent change, and `bun run test:metrics` supplies the measured post-change metric artifact once.
**4. Why `test-metrics.json` is in the set even though the freshness predicate will not red.** Removing tests changes the population but not the test-file list, and `artifactIsStale` keys only on the file list and the committed artifact's internal sum. Measured 2026-09-28 UTC on a disposable copy with tests removed: `bun test scripts/test-metrics.test.ts -t "the artifact is fresh"` still exits 0. So the artifact would keep the removed test names silently. This bundle regenerates it from a removed stale artifact and pins the relation, not a figure.
**5. The concurrent-worker `ChangeDetector` is a different design.** Its future interface identifies changes between each dedicated worker workspace and its baseline, with Git as its first replaceable implementation. It is not implemented or decided here; it belongs to its own concurrency artifact, which will present its own sequence and class diagrams before its brief. Keeping it out is what makes this slice small.
**6. The declaration-count guard (`AC-COVERAGE-INTACT`) is retired, and what it did and did not provide.** Applied `AC-COVERAGE-INTACT` (`.ngrace/changes/archive/C-TEST-TIME-BUDGET-4-F173437E/spec.xml`) required that no `*.test.ts` at HEAD carry fewer `it(`/`test(` declarations than base `2434fd467458e15c12414a74e37b09f9d71bdfd2`, read via `git show <base>:<path>`, to stop test deletion during the time-budget optimization. It measured **textual declaration count in existing files**, not executed code: it never observed executed statements, never a removed test body that kept its declaration, never a newly dead branch, and never a file absent at the base. Its history read **fails open**: `coverageRegressions` (`scripts/audit-regressions.test.ts:346`) `continue`s when `git show` exits non-zero (`:352`), so in a depth-1 checkout — where `2434fd4…` is absent — zeroing every declaration in a disposable `*.test.ts` left the guard green (a false green); after `git fetch --unshallow` the same mutation reddened, and a byte restore greened. A permanent shallow `validate` job would therefore carry a false green. Retiring it leaves **no broad suite-wide coverage floor**: the targeted current-code mint race test proves one behavior, not suite-wide coverage, and this spec does not claim it replaces a coverage measure. Measured executed-code coverage is a later, separate small bundle, with its rationale recorded in project-specific memory outside this repository; this bundle implements no coverage tooling.

Assumptions.Assumption: Measured 2026-09-28 UTC on base `80cc36f789dc35ef789cfe6d753a39e7115dce76`: the retained race test (`bun test --timeout=0 src/grace-generate.test.ts -t "AC-MINT-EXCLUSIVE: the repaired tree refuses"`) exits 0; `src/grace-generate.test.ts` held 58 tests and `scripts/audit-regressions.test.ts` held 97 tests in the committed `test-metrics.json`; `6dd1d95` and `2434fd4…` are ancestors of `HEAD`; `b53d13d…`, `0fbd5996…`, and `73044f83…` are reachable from no current ref but their objects are present in this clone (`git cat-file -e` succeeds). The three retirements reduce those per-file counts; the post-change `test-metrics.json` total is re-measured at regeneration, never projected. Counts expire when a bundle archives, so the close re-measures.

The removed historical control is the only hard `fetch-depth: 0` consumer in the `validate` job; the consumer search is recorded in `Constraints`. If the close finds a second hard consumer, the depth removal is refused rather than weakening that consumer.

The one-time red control's exact mutation is the pre-repair defect pair. The executor may choose a different minimal mutation that drives the retained test to red, provided it drives it to red and restores byte-identical, and provided the mutation stays out of the suite.
